correctness.rationale: The published linear-kernel definitions reduce exactly to \(T_n=\operatorname{sgn}(f_2)(n-2)C/\sqrt{n(n-1)Q}\). Gaussian centering makes the residual directions independent Haar points on the sphere of the sum-zero subspace, so the statistic is a constant times \(|u\cdot v|/\|P(u\circ v)\|\). For \(n=3\), the denominator is constant and the numerator is a cosine of a uniform angle difference, giving the arcsine law. For \(n\ge4\), the displayed reciprocal-coordinate zeros have nonzero numerator; the rank-three certificate at \(n=4\) and the five-distinct-coordinate quartic argument for \(n\ge5\) make the denominator map a submersion. A tube around its zero manifold therefore has probability of order at least \(t^{-(n-1)}\), and the tail integral gives the moment divergence. The actual verifier was inspected and independently confirms the algebraic reduction and rank certificates.

value.rationale: The theorem exposes a sharp finite-sample pathology of a statistic introduced specifically to enable Gaussian calibration: at the smallest admissible sizes the law changes from bounded arcsine to polynomially heavy with divergent high moments. This is a natural and practically relevant boundary fact, not an arbitrary finite calculation.
residual_risks: The result does not quantify moderate-tail calibration error at larger n.

final_claim: For scalar linear kernels under an independent nondegenerate Gaussian null, the published studentized cross-HSIC statistic has the arcsine law when the half-sample size is \(n=3\); for every fixed \(n\ge4\) it has unbounded support with \(\Pr(|T_n|>t)\ge c_n t^{-(n-1)}\) for all sufficiently large \(t\), so \(\mathbb E|T_n|^p=\infty\) for every \(p\ge n-1\).
limitations: Scalar linear kernels and independent Gaussian coordinates only.
The tail bound is one-sided; no exact tail constant or matching upper bound is claimed.
Moment finiteness below order \(n-1\) is not determined.
